# Generated by src/codegen/lint-rule-docs.ts. Do not edit below this line.

React can render a component more than once for one update, and it can reuse an earlier result. So a component must return the same output for the same props and state. A call that returns a new value each time breaks that. The id, the time, or the random number changes on every render, and the server and the browser disagree during hydration.

The rule reports `Math.random()`, `Date.now()`, and `performance.now()` in the body of a component or a hook. Calls in event handlers and effects are fine, because they don't run during render.

With an oxlint config, the rule also reports `new Date()` and `Date()` without arguments.

{/* Generated by src/codegen/lint-rule-docs.ts. Do not edit this section. */}

## Configure

Off by default. To turn it on:

```toml bunfig.toml
[lint.rules]
"react-hooks/purity" = "error" # or "warn"
```

{/* End of the generated section. */}

## Examples

Reported:

{/* bad */}
```jsx
function Clock() {
  const now = Date.now();
  return <time>{now}</time>;
}
```

{/* bad */}
```jsx
function Field({ label }) {
  const id = Math.random();
  return <input id={id} aria-label={label} />;
}
```

Not reported:

{/* good */}
```jsx
import { useEffect, useId, useState } from "react";

function Clock() {
  const [now, setNow] = useState(() => Date.now());
  useEffect(() => {
    const timer = setInterval(() => setNow(Date.now()), 1000);
    return () => clearInterval(timer);
  }, []);
  return <time>{now}</time>;
}

function Field({ label }) {
  const id = useId();
  return <input id={id} aria-label={label} />;
}
```
